title: Geographic Subdivision to the City Level
summary: The "city flip" (expressing certain topics in cities as [city]--[topic] instead of [topic]--[place]--[city]) was discontinued in 1985. Any heading authorized for geographic subdivision is now divided to the city level (e.g. Fountains--California --Los Angeles). Additional [city]--[topic] headings may be assigned for local history, structures (--Buildings, structures, etc.), the city as a topic, and historical treatments of events.
validation_rules: If a heading is authorized for geographic subdivision, divide it geographically to the city level for a topic in a specific city: `Fountains--California--Los Angeles` (not the former city-flip form `Los Angeles (Calif.)--Fountains`). (H 832 sec. 1)

The city flip, discontinued in 1985, formerly applied to the topics listed in the Background; strings such as `[city]--Fountains`, `[city]--Bridges`, `[city]--Parks` that rely on it are obsolete unless the subdivision is otherwise valid under city names (H 1140). (H 832 Background)
For local history and genealogy works, an additional `[city]--[topic]` heading may also be assigned (H 1845). (H 832 sec. 2)
For categories of structures (buildings, monuments, bridges, etc.), also assign `[city]--Buildings, structures, etc.` within the limits of H 1334 and H 1334.5. (H 832 sec. 3)

If the city is an important aspect of the work, assign an additional `[city]--[topic]` heading using a subdivision valid under city names (e.g. `--Race relations`, `--Social life and customs`; H 1140). (H 832 sec. 4)

For disasters, riots, demonstrations, etc. in cities, assign `[category of event]--[place]`, and for historical treatments `[city]--History--[period or century subdivision, if appropriate]` (H 1560). (H 832 sec. 5)

sections.heading: 1. General rule
sections.text: If a work discusses a topic in a specific city, and the heading for the topic is authorized for geographic subdivision, divide the heading geographically to the city level, for example, *Fountains--California--Los Angeles*.

sections.heading: 2. Local history materials
sections.text: For works of interest to local historians and genealogists, also assign an appropriate [city]--[topic] heading, as described in H 1845.

sections.heading: 3. Structures
sections.text: If the topic of the work is a category of structures, such as buildings, monuments, bridges, etc., also assign the heading [city]--Buildings, structures, etc., within the limitations of H 1334 and H 1334.5.

sections.heading: 4. City as topic of work
sections.text: If the city is judged to be an important aspect of the work in its own right, assign an additional heading of the type [city]--[topic], using one of the topical subdivisions valid for use under city names, for example, --Race relations, --Social life and customs, etc. (cf. H 1140).

sections.heading: 5. Works about disasters, riots, demonstrations, etc., in cities
sections.text: As a general rule, assign a heading of the type [category of event]--[place], and for historical treatments, a heading of the type [city]--History--[period or century subdivision, if appropriate] (see H 1560).
